chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, he said:

I asked him about the ground and the roof that urine or something similar reaches: does the sun purify it without water? He said: How can it become pure without water? The proper understanding of this report is that it does not become pure without water so long as it remains wet. Rather, purity is judged for it when the sun has dried it.

key_terms.السَّطْحِ: the roof or elevated surface mentioned alongside the ground
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose drying effect is central to the ruling
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the ground or earth surface under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, the impurity affecting the surface
key_terms.جَفَّفَتْهُ: dried it, referring to the sun drying the impure surface
key_terms.رَطْبًا: wet; the state in which purity is not judged to occur
key_terms.طَهَارَتِهِ: its purity, meaning the legal judgment of ritual cleanliness
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water, the normal means of purification being contrasted here

ai.seo_question: Does the sun purify ground or a roof affected by urine without water?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of ritual purity regarding ground or rooftops affected by urine or similar impurity. It indicates that such a surface is not considered pure without water while it remains wet, and that a ruling of purity applies once the sun has dried it.
